critical.name: Freeze after a relink is refused: the round base tag is re-requested on the relinked base
critical.summary:
plan.py new tags base/<stem>/r1 on the original base A. relink re-points base_commit to B and tags base/<stem>/r1-2, leaving r1 on A (test_relink_repoints_base_commit asserts exactly that). The next freeze, first or --refreeze, calls freeze_pending -> base_tags(stem, plan.base_commit) and asks for base/<stem>/r1 -> B. freeze_git.preflight finds r1 already peeling to A and raises 'tag ... already points at A, not B', so the freeze is refused before it writes anything. Every relinked plan is stuck: the documented route of unlock, write, freeze --refreeze and then lock never gets past the freeze, and only deleting the tag by hand unblocks it. strap_lock.freeze_pending has the same defect: reopen tags base/skill/<name>/r<N> on the old base, relink tags r<N>-2 on the new one, and the next freeze in that round asks for r<N> on spec.base and is refused (test_relink_repoints_base_and_tags sets up exactly this state and stops before a freeze). No test runs a freeze after a relink.

Also (overall): relink keeps the old tag base/<stem>/r1 on the old base and adds base/<stem>/r1-<m> on the new one (plan_lock.py:507-511; test_plan_lock.py:338-339 asserts both). The next freeze re-adds the fixed name: freeze_pending builds base_tags(stem, plan.base_commit), i.e. base/<stem>/r1 -> the new base_commit (plan_lock.py:166-168, 299-300), and freeze_git._conflict reports 'tag base/<stem>/r1 already points at <old>, not <new>', so preflight refuses the command. So once a plan is relinked, plan.py freeze --refreeze can never run again: not on a Frozen plan, and not after unlock --arm / unlock on a Locked one. That breaks the documented path 'unlock, write, freeze --refreeze, lock' (write-plan SKILL.md, Relink and Unlock). strap_lock.freeze_pending has the same defect: after strap.py relink in round N it adds base/skill/<name>/rN -> spec.base (the new base), which conflicts with the tag new --edit, reopen or the first freeze left on the old base (strap_lock.py:208-209). No test runs relink followed by a refreeze, so the suite stays green.

Also (roast): relink re-points base_commit (plan) or base (strap) and tags the new commit base/<stem>/r<N>-<m>, leaving base/<stem>/r<N> on the old commit. The next freeze then rebuilds the plain round tag from the current base: plan_lock.freeze_pending puts base_tags(stem, plan.base_commit) = {base/<stem>/r1: <new base>} into preflight, and strap_lock.freeze_pending adds base/skill/<name>/r<N> -> spec.base. freeze_git._conflict finds r<N> already on the old commit, so preflight refuses with 'tag base/... already points at <old>, not <new>'. Three cases hit this: a relinked Frozen plan's freeze --refreeze, the refreeze after unlock on a relinked Locked plan, and the first freeze of a plan relinked before it was ever frozen (plan.py new already tagged r1). A strap spec's refreeze after a part change in the same round hits it too. The whole feature exists for the rebase case, and after that one rebase the subject cannot freeze again until someone deletes a tag by hand. test_plan_relink_lock.py and test_strap_relink_lock.py stop at lock and check and never refreeze.
fix: Request the round base tag only when no existing base/<stem>/r<N>[-<m>] tag already peels to the current base: in plan_lock.base_tags/freeze_pending and strap_lock.freeze_pending, list the base tags of the round (the _base_ms prefix) and drop the r<N> request when one of them holds the base. Add a test that runs relink and then freeze --refreeze for plans and for strap specs.
Alternatively, have freeze tag the base the ledger already knows: skip the base tag whenever a relink entry of the round names the current base as new_base, since relink already tagged it.

In plan_lock.freeze_pending and strap_lock.freeze_pending, add a base tag only when no existing base/<stem>/r<N>[-<m>] tag already peels to the current base (reuse _base_ms / the tag --list scan _base_lines already does), and never re-target the fixed r<N> name once it exists on another object. Add a driver test for each: relink, then freeze --refreeze (plan: also after unlock --arm / unlock), expecting exit 0 and no new base tag.
Alternatively record the base tag name in the relink entry and have freeze_pending reuse the latest relink's tag name instead of base_tag(stem, round).

Make the freeze's base tag relink-aware: when any existing base/<stem>/r<N> or base/<stem>/r<N>-<m> tag already peels to the current base, add no base tag (or use that name); create base/<stem>/r<N> only when no tag of the round holds the base. Apply the same rule in plan_lock.freeze_pending / base_tags and strap_lock.freeze_pending, and add driver tests: relink, then freeze --refreeze succeeds (plan Frozen, plan unlocked after a relinked lock, never-frozen plan, strap spec in the same round).

important.name: guard_locked lets a session delete or move ledger entries, which undoes a lock
important.summary:
The module docstring says every file under <plans>/freezes/ is denied, but the only shapes it extracts are write destinations: Bash redirects, tee, sed -i and the cp/mv destination; PowerShell redirects, Set-Content/Add-Content/Out-File and the Copy-Item/Move-Item destination. Three commands reach the ledger anyway: 'rm docs/plans/freezes/plan/0001-x/r1.3-lock.json', 'mv <that file> /tmp/', where only the /tmp destination is checked, and 'Remove-Item <that file>'. Each one removes the lock entry. freeze_ledger.state then reads the plan as Frozen, and plan_api.write, freeze --refreeze and the guard's own locked_paths all treat it as editable. That is the most direct way past a Locked plan or spec, with no developer OK involved.

Also (roast): guard_locked counts only write destinations. _copy_targets returns the cp/mv destination and never the mv source, and _bash_segment does not handle rm, unlink or git rm at all. _PS_WRITERS has no Remove-Item (ri, del, erase, rm) and treats Move-Item like Copy-Item, so its source is skipped too. A Bash call like `rm docs/plans/freezes/plan/<stem>/r1.2-lock.json`, or an mv of that file out of the plans folder, therefore passes the hook. fl.state then drops back to frozen, and plan_api.write and freeze --refreeze accept the plan with no arm entry. That is the exact route the two-step unlock exists to close, and it is cheaper to type than any write the guard does catch. The 'best-effort' label covers clever shapes, not the most obvious one.
fix: Treat deletion and move sources under <plans>/freezes/ (and Locked paths) as targets: rm/unlink and the cp/mv sources in _bash_segment, git rm/git mv, and Remove-Item/ri/del/erase plus the Move-Item source in _PS_WRITERS. Add tests in the guard_locked hook test.
If deletion is deliberately out of scope, say so in the module docstring and in _WAY_IN, so the claim that every file under freezes/ is denied matches what the hook does.

Treat as targets the operands of rm/unlink/git rm (Bash), the sources of mv and git mv, and the -Path/-LiteralPath or positional operands of Remove-Item and its aliases plus the Move-Item source (PowerShell). Add cases to tests/hooks/test_guard_locked.py for each shape on a ledger entry and on a Locked plan JSON.

important.name: ledger stem pattern rejects stems that freeze builds from hand-named plan files
important.summary: The new `ledger` property only accepts `^plan/[0-9]{4}-[A-Za-z0-9-]+$`, but `plan.py freeze` builds the stem with `stem_of` -> `file_slug` -> `stem_slug` (plan_lock.py:61-76). That code only swaps `_` for `-` and lowercases whatever sits between `<id>_` and `_ActionPlan.json`. The schema README accepts any `{NNNN}_*_ActionPlan.json` name, so a hand-named file with a dot, plus sign, comma or non-ASCII letter (`0012_v1.2_fix_ActionPlan.json`) gives `plan/0012-v1.2-fix`. `write_freeze` assigns it to `plan.ledger` with no assignment validation, saves the JSON, writes the ledger entries and tags (git ref names allow those characters), and reports success. The next load then fails the schema pattern, so the plan is frozen in the ledger but its JSON can no longer be read. `todo_sync/rules_plans.py:25` copies the same narrow pattern, so a plan with such a stem also drops out of todo sync.
fix: Normalize the slug in `stem_slug`/`file_slug` to the stem alphabet, e.g. `re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", slug.lower()).strip("-")`, so every built stem matches the `ledger` pattern; add a test that freezes a plan file whose title holds a dot.
Or validate `pending.stem` against the `ActionPlan.ledger` pattern in `freeze_pending` before any write and fail with a problem line naming the file.

important.name: No behavioral test that the three dispatchers apply the lock guard's deny
important.summary:
The guard reaches a session only through write_pretool.py, bash_pretool.py and powershell_pretool.py, and guard_locked.py's docstring promises it runs first there, so its deny outranks any allow the other hooks would give. No test checks this. test_guard_locked.py calls guard.decide directly, and its registration test (test_dispatchers_registered_and_compose_guard_locked) only regex-matches an `import guard_locked` line, which test_hooks_json_paths.py::test_a_dispatcher_imports_exactly_its_composed_hooks already checks more strictly. test_bash_pretool.py never mentions guard_locked, and write_pretool.py and powershell_pretool.py have no test file. A dispatcher that imports guard_locked but skips it, runs it after an allow, or swallows its output would pass every test in the suite.

Also (tests): The module docstring says the guard denies a write to any path that a Locked or armed subject's ledger lists. test_sealed_plan_json_stays_writable_under_lock asserts the opposite for a plan whose lock carries the sealed scheme or no scheme: the plan JSON stays writable and only the planned test is denied. guard_locked.py documents this exception at lines 10-11; the test module does not.
fix: Replace test_dispatchers_registered_and_compose_guard_locked with behavioral tests. On the _project seed, load each dispatcher by path and call its decide(). Assert 'deny' for a Write to LOCKED_PLAN through write_pretool, a Bash redirect into a ledger file through bash_pretool, and a Set-Content onto LOCKED_PLAN through powershell_pretool. Add one case per dispatcher where the other composed hook would allow the same command (an allow-listed Bash or PowerShell shape that writes into a locked path), to pin the precedence.
Keep the hooks.json matcher asserts if wanted, but drop the import-regex check: it duplicates the contract test.
Add a sentence to the module docstring: a plan whose lock carries the sealed scheme or no scheme keeps its plan JSON writable, since record still writes it, while its other locked files stay denied.

minor.name: guard_locked plans-folder match ignores the Windows case rule and MSYS drive paths
minor.summary:
_under compares in the OS's case rule and _key lowercases on nt, but decide() filters with a case-sensitive r.startswith(plans_rel + '/'), and _verdict checks rel.startswith(freezes) the same way. On Windows, a Write to 'Docs/Plans/...' when the config says docs/plans skips the guard. A Git Bash path such as '/e/proj/docs/plans/...' is not absolute on Windows either, so repo_rel joins it under cwd and returns None. Both are silent bypasses of a deny-only guard.

Also (overall): repo_rel treats a target as absolute only when Path(...).is_absolute(). On Windows a Git Bash path such as /e/repo/docs/plans/freezes/plan/x/r1.1-freeze.json has no drive, so it is joined onto cwd (E:/e/repo/...), falls outside the project root and returns None. The Bash tool on Windows runs Git Bash, where such paths are routine, so 'echo x > /e/<repo>/docs/plans/freezes/...' or 'tee /c/...' onto a Locked file passes the guard. The guard is best-effort by design, but this is the shell form the Bash tool most often emits on Windows.
fix: Compare through _key on both sides (_key(r).startswith(_key(plans_rel) + '/') and the same for the freezes prefix). In repo_rel, map a leading '/<letter>/' to '<letter>:/' on nt before resolving.

In repo_rel, on os.name == 'nt' map a leading '/<letter>/' (and '/cygdrive/<letter>/') to '<letter>:/' before the absolute test, and add a Windows-path case to tests/hooks/test_guard_locked.py marked cross_os.
